title: Copy pi's packages/evals into omp as @oh-my-pi/pi-evals
one_line: pi's behavioural eval harness for its coding agent — it measures whether the agent can configure its OWN installation (add a provider, add a model, create a tool extension) with and without the repo's documentation shipped, by running paired arms in two throwaway Docker images; it is the only thing in pi that tells you a change broke agent behaviour, and roughly 40% of it is Docker/vitest/pi-release-layout plumbing that omp has to be rebuilt rather than copied.
why_copy_not_reimplement: Three things here are expensive to re-derive and cheap to copy. (1) The paired-comparison statistics in src/report.ts: 483 lines that implement 'a pair contributes to lift only when BOTH arms produce exactly one score; any missing, duplicate, skipped, pending, unscored or errored arm blocks the pair; if any pair in an eval set is blocked the headline is withheld; missing telemetry is unavailable, never zero'. That is a protocol argument, not code — six independent blocking rules that had to be reasoned into existence against real noisy model output. Re-deriving it means rediscovering every rule by being burned by it. (2) The container sandbox in src/harness.ts L130-188: chmod 0600 on every transformed module under tmpdir, chownTree the workspace to a throwaway uid, verify the demoted process cannot read its own evaluator, then delete the credential env var. That is adversarial hardening against the agent under test reading its own grader — again, the kind of thing you only get right after an incident. (3) The whole measurement design: the agent configures a LIVE running installation and is then graded on the RESULT via a fake provider server, with alternated arm ordering to de-bias, a protocol digest binding every report to its exact plan, and a nonzero exit when pairs block. Meanwhile omp today has zero behavioural eval of its coding agent — packages/coding-agent/src/eval/ is a JS/Python sandbox executor with a completely different meaning of 'eval', and the nearest thing to a bench (packages/typescript-edit-benchmark) measures edit mechanics, not agent judgement. So the gap is real. The counter-argument is also real: the expensive half is the harness, the copyable half is the plumbing, and the plumbing is the part that has to be thrown away. The honest shape of this migration is copy the ~30% that is judgement and statistics, rebuild the ~70% that is Docker, vitest, and pi's release-tarball layout.

collisions.what: readStoredCredential — SAME NAME, DIFFERENT SIGNATURE. pi: readStoredCredential(provider, authPath) at packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:496. omp: readStoredCredential(provider) at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/legacy-pi-coding-agent-shim.ts:1469, which resolves auth.json through AuthStorage.create() and takes no path.
collisions.resolution: KEEP omp's. The whole point of the eval harness is to read a credential from an ISOLATED agent dir before the session exists; omp's version reads the process-global AuthStorage and would silently use the developer's real ~/.omp/agent/auth.json — leaking the developer's credentials into a container that then drops privileges. omp's signature is also the one the 2-arg call would compile against only by accident. Resolve the path explicitly (authPath = join(hostAgentDir,'auth.json')) and read the file directly, or add an optional second parameter to omp's function.

collisions.what: CreateAgentSessionOptions.tools / .noTools DO NOT EXIST in omp. pi's harness types PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions.tools and .noTools as CreateAgentSessionOptions['tools'] / ['noTools'] and forwards them to createAgentSessionFromServices. omp's CreateAgentSessionOptions (packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts:495) has customTools and extensions but neither tools nor noTools.
collisions.resolution: KEEP omp's interface; retype the harness options to plain `string[]` and map them onto omp's session construction. The 6 DOCUMENTATION_EVAL_TOOLS names ('read','write','edit','grep','find','ls') must be verified to exist in omp's tool registry under those names — if omp renamed any, the control arm silently runs with a smaller toolset, which is exactly the kind of quiet protocol violation these evals exist to prevent.

collisions.what: ModelRuntime does not exist anywhere in omp. pi: packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:153. omp has no packages/coding-agent/src/core/ at all. This breaks resolveModelSelection's downstream (ModelRuntime.create/getModel/getAuth/setRuntimeApiKey) AND all of evals/configured-runtime.ts.
collisions.omp_anchor: mới — không có (nearest: packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts:495 authStorage/modelRegistry, and packages/catalog's model manager)
collisions.resolution: BLOCKING for the model-probing evals, non-blocking for the rest. Do NOT create a ModelRuntime shim to make the copy compile. Repoint at omp's ModelRegistry + AuthStorage + getModel and accept that models.docs.eval.ts / openai-provider.docs.eval.ts / custom-provider.docs.eval.ts (3 of 5 eval suites) are out of scope until that reconcile lands. Ship report.ts + plan.ts + acme-server.ts + the 4 porting tests first.

collisions.what: createAgentSessionServices / createAgentSessionFromServices do not exist in omp. pi: packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session-services.ts:135,202. omp's createAgentSession (packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts:1485) is the single entry point and returns {session, ...} directly, with no separately-constructed services object.
collisions.resolution: KEEP omp's createAgentSession. The two-step services/attach shape is pi's plugin architecture; omp's opts out. The harness must pass cwd/agentDir/model/thinkingLevel/customTools/extensions in one call. Verify session.reload() and session.abort() still exist on the returned AgentSession — harness.ts L376 and L370 depend on both, and 'reload' is the step that makes the configure-your-own-installation evals possible.

collisions.what: InlineExtension does not exist in omp; omp calls the same concept ExtensionFactory, and the event name used to rewrite the system prompt differs. pi's harness registers a hidden inline extension listening for 'before_agent_start' and replacing the prompt.
collisions.resolution: KEEP omp's ExtensionFactory. But do NOT assume the hook name carries over: verify the actual omp hook for pre-prompt system-prompt rewriting. If none exists, add one — this is a legitimate gap, because the entire with_docs/without_docs experiment is defined by a system-prompt difference, and a prompt-rewriting seam is required for ANY doc-lift measurement. Note pi's comment at L388-389: a forced prompt is not recorded in the transcript, which is why the harness keeps the transform's own value.

collisions.what: getDocsPath / getExamplesPath / getReadmePath do not exist in omp (0 definitions, verified). test/harness.test.ts imports all three to assert the doc files a variant should or should not have.
collisions.resolution: REPLACE, do not re-add. The doc-path helpers pi used are not omp's API. Derive the expected doc paths from omp's own `packages/coding-agent` package.json `files` array, which is the shipped contract — and note it already lists `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `examples` but has NO `docs` entry, unlike pi's.

collisions.what: The 'docs' directory the whole experiment strips does not exist in the same place. pi deletes packages/coding-agent/{README.md,CHANGELOG.md,docs,examples} in the without_docs image and asserts on exactly that set. omp's coding-agent ships README.md, CHANGELOG.md, examples/ — and no docs/; its user-facing docs live at repo-root ./docs, and its bundle carries an omp-only dist/docs-index.generated.txt that backs the omp:// docs URL scheme.
collisions.resolution: RETARGET the doc set, do not delete the concept. The without_docs arm must strip exactly what omp's model can actually see: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, examples/, and dist/docs-index.generated.txt (the omp-only one — stripping it is a NEW arm pi had no equivalent of, and dropping it would leave the treatment reading docs the control cannot). Separately, documentation-audit.eval.ts globs a directory that does not exist in omp and would discover ZERO cases — a silent no-op, the worst failure mode in the package. Either repoint it at omp's real docs or do not port it.

collisions.what: pi's release-tarball install pipeline has no omp equivalent. install-runtime.mjs imports getPublicWorkspacePackages/packReleasePackages/installCodingAgentConsumer from scripts/release-packages.mjs and scripts/coding-agent-consumer.mjs — neither file exists in omp. It then installs the packed tarballs and entrypoint.ts asserts pi-coding-agent resolves to dist/index.js with an npm-shrinkwrap.json present.
collisions.omp_anchor: mới — không có (omp scripts/ has ci-release-*.ts + release.ts, which publish from source; coding-agent's main is ./src/index.ts and its only dist artifact is dist/cli.js)
collisions.resolution: REBUILD, do not port. There is no npm-installable compiled runtime in omp to image. The realistic options are (a) mount the omp workspace source into the container and run the CLI from source with bun — losing the 'resolves from dist' guarantee but gaining fidelity to how developers actually run omp; or (b) extend scripts/release.ts to emit packed tarballs and write the missing consumer helper. Recommend (a) for a first cut: it is smaller, it cannot drift from the source, and the dist-resolution assertion it drops is a pi-release-specific check, not a security control.

collisions.what: The 'eval' name collides with a large, unrelated omp subsystem. packages/coding-agent/src/eval/ is 60 files of JS/Python sandbox execution, kernel sessions, speculation evaluators and workpool bridges; packages/coding-agent/src/if-bench/ and src/judgment/ sit next to it. A new packages/evals at repo root does not collide on disk, but 'eval' in an omp code review now means two unrelated things.
collisions.resolution: KEEP both, but name the concept in prose. The new package evaluates AGENT BEHAVIOUR (does the agent configure its own installation correctly); the existing eval/ subsystem evaluates UNTRUSTED CODE the agent wrote. Call the new one 'behavioural evals' in docs, changelog and commit messages, and never add it to scripts/ci-test-ts.ts's existing `eval`-named buckets without a comment. Consider a packages/evals/README.md line that says so on the first page.

collisions.what: vitest does not exist in omp at all — 13 import sites, 2 config files, 1 reporter invocation, and a root vitest.base.ts that omp does not have. The entire runner, the project split, and the discovery mechanism (`vitest list --json`) are vitest-specific.
collisions.omp_anchor: mới — không có (omp: bun test via scripts/ci-test-ts.ts, which globs `*.test.ts` and buckets packages by name)
collisions.resolution: REPLACE with bun:test for the unit tests — omp's ci-test-ts.ts already collects any `*.test.ts` under a package dir, so 4 test files port by changing one import line each. The docker-arm runner has no bun equivalent and is the reason the comparison runner is rewrite-only. Do not add vitest.

collisions.what: session.resourceLoader does not exist on omp's AgentSession. extensions.docs.eval.ts reads session.resourceLoader.getExtensions() for both the loaded-extension list and the per-extension tool sets. omp exposes session.extensionRunner (a getter at packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:12155) but no resourceLoader.
collisions.resolution: REPOINT to omp's extension surface once identified; extensionRunner may be optional (returns `ExtensionRunner | undefined`), so the ported output mapper must handle the undefined case rather than assume it. This eval is the most valuable of the five (it proves an agent can create and then use a tool extension), so it is worth the extra work — but it is a rewrite, not a copy.

files_to_copy.rewrite: No rewrite. Zero @earendil-works, zero node builtins, zero vitest imports — the only file that ports byte-for-byte. Rewrite 6 import lines only: L4 `node:util` styleText -> `Bun.styleText`; L5-6 `@vitest-evals/core` + `/node` imports -> new local `./report-io.ts` (see new files); L7 unchanged. Everything else — pairing, blocking, flags, formatters — is pure and ports unchanged.

L6 `await requireEvalAuthFile(...)` -> add `await`. Rewrite the 3 `console.log` calls: the rule bans `console.*` while TUI/RPC/SDK live, but a standalone CLI that exits without entering the TUI IS the documented exception — so these 3 are ALLOWED as-is; do not convert to `logger` (logger writes to ~/.omp/logs, not the user's terminal, and would break the runner's output contract). Change the hardcoded container prefix `/repo/packages/evals/` (L101) to read from the resolved packageRoot. Everything else ports unchanged.

THE hard file — 4 of its 9 external symbols do not exist in omp. (b) L9 `getCurrentSystemPrompt` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/utils/transcript` -> local `./system-prompt.ts` re-implementation over omp's `Message`. test_contract:
Four things must be observably true after the migration, and each has exactly one test that proves it.

(1) BLOCKING PROPAGATION. Given a planned cohort where one arm errored, zero was discovered, or two arms share an identity, summarizeEvalObservations must list that pair in blockedPairs, set that eval set's controlPassRate and treatmentPassRate to null, and set lift to null — and must NOT silently drop the pair from the denominator. Proven by test/comparison.test.ts.

(2) A DISAPPEARED METRIC IS UNAVAILABLE, NOT ZERO. readTaskObservation on a report missing a telemetry field must produce outcome:'errored' or a summary whose OperationalMetricTotal carries {availableRuns: n, total: null} — never total: 0. Zero cost and unmeasured cost are different facts and conflating them makes a regression look free. Proven by test/report.test.ts and test/comparison.test.ts.

(3) THE ARM SANDBOX IS REAL. The evaluator's own source and fixtures must be unreadable by the uid the harness demotes to, and the demotion must be permanent. This is asserted in-process by the chmod/chownTree/assertSandboxCannotRead trio and end-to-end by docker/entrypoint.ts. In the first cut (source-mounted, no image), the in-process half still must hold or the eval grades a model that can read its grader.

(4) AN ARM THAT PRODUCED NO REPORT IS AN ERRORED OBSERVATION, NOT A MISSING ONE. runTask returning undefined must produce erroredObservation(task) so the pair blocks and the process exits nonzero — never a silently shorter denominator, which would report lift computed over a cohort the protocol did not plan. Proven by test/comparison.test.ts and the cli.ts exit-code path.

Plus the runner-agnostic invariants that survive the vitest->bun swap: the acme fixture server rejects 404/405/415/400/422/401 distinctly; createTaskPlan alternates arm order by run number; parseDiscoveredCases rejects a name without "<eval set> > <case>" and rejects duplicate identities.

NOT a contract, and must not be tested: that the harness constructor stores its options, that constants have particular values, that the report is non-empty, that a file exists. No source-grepping. No mock.module(). applyIsolatedEnvironment mutates process.env and registerEvalCleanup() runs in omp's createAgentSession, so the harness test must use per-test vi.spyOn + vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach rather than a file-wide mutation.

risk:
Highest: the SILENT NO-OP. Three concrete ways this migration can succeed at every gate and still measure nothing. (a) The without_docs arm strips a docs set that does not exist in omp — pi deletes packages/coding-agent/docs, omp has no such directory, so a copied Dockerfile would strip nothing and the control arm would read the same documentation as the treatment. (b) verifySystemPrompt and excludePiDocumentation key on pi's literal `\n<docs>\nPi documentation (read only` and `\n<rules>\n` markers; if omp's prompt layout differs, the assertion either throws (visible) or the stripper returns the prompt unchanged (invisible). (c) DOCUMENTATION_EVAL_TOOLS names 6 tools that may not exist under those names in omp, so the arm runs with a smaller toolset and the comparison is between two differently-equipped agents. All three fail closed on nothing — no error, no nonzero exit, just a wrong number. Mitigate by asserting the two arms' system prompts actually differ before recording any observation, and by making the image's doc-strip list assert-then-delete rather than delete-if-present.

Second: the credential leak. Copying harness.ts's readStoredCredential call as-is would either not compile (good) or, if someone 'fixes' it by dropping the authPath argument, would silently read the developer's real ~/.omp/agent/auth.json and ship their credential into a container that then drops to an unprivileged uid. This is the one defect in this migration that could cost something real, and the fix is a one-line discipline: never call omp's 1-arg readStoredCredential from the harness.

Third: the vitest question. The tempting shortcut is to add vitest so the copy runs unchanged. Reject it — omp is a bun test repo, adding a second runner to one package creates two test systems with different configs, different lifecycles, and different CI plumbing, and it will be read as a mistake. The 4 unit-test files port with one import line each; that is the cheap part. The docker-arm runner genuinely has no bun equivalent, and that should be a stated limitation, not a reason to reintroduce vitest.

Fourth: scope. It is tempting to port all 5 eval suites to 'complete' the package. Three of them test whether an agent can add a provider or a model to its OWN installation — a capability omp may not have at all, because omp replaced pi's provider-registration surface with a KDL rule tree compiled at build time. If the capability is gone, the eval is unwriteable, and writing it anyway would produce an eval that can never pass. Verify the capability exists before porting the suite.
open_questions: Does omp's coding-agent support an agent adding a provider or model to its own installation at all? pi's 3 of 5 eval suites (models, openai-provider, custom-provider) test exactly that. omp's model policy lives in a compiled KDL rule tree (packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/), not in a runtime-editable registry — if so those 3 evals are unwriteable and the package ships with 2 behavioural suites instead of 5. THIS BLOCKS THE SCOPE DECISION and should be answered before any suite is ported.

Is a narrower harness test (the pure parts: resolveModelSelection, verifySystemPrompt, resolveDocumentationVariant, excludePiDocumentation, seedWorkspace's escape rejection) worth writing against bun:test, or does the AGENTS.md test-quality bar rule it out as too narrow?

The other 6 new packages are unaffected (chord, client, durable, protocol, server, telemetry) but if evals is the one that looks wrong, now is the time — after it lands it is a breaking change to a published package name.

Option (a) mount omp source into a bun container and run from source (smaller, cannot drift, loses pi's dist-resolution assertion); option (b) extend scripts/release.ts to emit packed tarballs and write the missing scripts/release-packages.mjs + scripts/coding-agent-consumer.mjs (faithful, bigger, and a new build surface to maintain). This is a maintainer decision with a long tail, and it should be made once, explicitly, not drifted into.

They are not deletable (they encode real contracts against a surface omp does not have yet) and leaving them unfiled means the next person re-derives that ModelRuntime is missing.
